items.question: What attainment makes a practitioner dear to the yoginīs?
premises: Enjoyment and liberation together constitute a great accomplishment.
Such accomplishment can arise for a practitioner.
Being dear to the yoginīs is a possible result.
items.inference: One who attains the great accomplishment of enjoyment and liberation may become dear to the yoginīs.
items.plain_english: He may become dear to the yoginīs through the great accomplishment of both enjoyment and liberation.

items.question: Which chapter concludes after emerging in the moon island?
premises: A chapter is identified by ordinal number.
The chapter is described as emerged in Candra-dvīpa.
The colophon marks its completion.
items.inference: The ninth chapter, having emerged in Candra-dvīpa, is concluded.
items.plain_english: Thus ends the ninth chapter, which emerged in Candra-dvīpa.

items.question: How should the practitioner visualize the self in this meditative posture?
premises: The self is to be visualized as surrounded by fire.
The self is to be visualized standing on one foot.
These details define a specific contemplative image.
items.inference: The practitioner should visualize the self encircled by fire and standing on one foot.
items.plain_english: One should visualize the self surrounded by fire and standing on one foot.

items.question: What revelation about knowledge is being requested from the deity?
premises: The speaker addresses the deity directly.
The speaker asks for the determination of knowledge.
The request is for immediate manifestation.
items.inference: The deity is asked to make manifest the determination of knowledge to the speaker now.
items.plain_english: O God, make manifest to me today the true determination of knowledge.

items.question: What complete division of octads does the seeker wish to understand?
premises: The subject is the division of eight octads.
The seeker desires full knowledge of this division.
The knowledge is sought in an exhaustive manner.
items.inference: The seeker wishes to know fully and exhaustively the division of the eight octads.
uncertainties: anantathā may indicate endless extent or thoroughness
items.plain_english: And I wish to know fully and completely the division of the eight octads.

items.question: How is accomplishment quickly attained in the secret place and wheel?
premises: A secret place is the locus of practice.
A wheel is associated with this practice.
Quick accomplishment is possible there.
items.inference: The secret place and its wheel are described as means by which accomplishment arises quickly.
items.plain_english: O Bhairava, tell me how the secret place and the wheel are quickly accomplished.

items.question: Why does the deity praise the question asked by the great goddess?
premises: The deity expresses strong approval.
The goddess has asked a question.
The subject asked about is hard for gods to obtain.
items.inference: The deity praises the goddess because she has asked about a matter difficult even for the gods.
items.plain_english: Well said, well said, O great goddess; you have asked me about something hard for even the gods to obtain.

items.question: Where are the syllables kṣa and laṃ located in the subtle body?
premises: The syllable kṣa is associated with the brahmarandhra.
The syllable laṃ is associated with the forehead.
Specific syllables are mapped to bodily locations.
items.inference: The syllable kṣa belongs to the brahmarandhra and the syllable laṃ to the forehead.
uncertainties: lalāṭayoḥ is dual in form though often used for the forehead region
items.plain_english: The syllable kṣa is in the brahmarandhra, and the syllable laṃ is in the forehead.

items.question: Where are the syllables ṣa and śa placed within the body?
premises: The syllable ṣa is assigned to the throat region.
The syllable śa is assigned to the heart.
These placements continue the mapping of syllables.
items.inference: The syllable ṣa is located in the throat region and the syllable śa in the heart.
items.plain_english: Then the syllable ṣa is in the throat region, and the syllable śa is in the heart.

items.question: What instruction follows after the place-wheels have been declared?
premises: The place-wheels have been declared.
Each has an associated meditation.
The listener is invited to hear about that meditation.
items.inference: After declaring the place-wheels, the teaching turns to their meditation.
items.plain_english: Thus the place-wheels have been declared; now hear their meditation, O beloved.

items.question: How is the divine lotus of the first octad to be visualized?
premises: The lotus is described as divine.
The lotus has eight spokes or petals.
It is adorned by the first octad.
items.inference: The meditation envisions a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.
uncertainties: āraṃ may indicate spokes or petals depending on context
items.plain_english: Visualize a divine eight-spoked lotus adorned by the first octad.

rows.grounds: object to be abandoned; sandhi form

items.question: What conduct should a practitioner with balanced mind abandon through practice?
premises: Practice leads to an even or balanced mind.
Village dharma represents conventional social conduct.
The practitioner is instructed to abandon it.
items.inference: Through practice, one with a balanced mind should abandon the dharma of village life.
uncertainties: grāma dharma may refer broadly to worldly or social obligations
items.plain_english: Through practice, with an even mind, one should abandon the ways of village life.

items.question: What yogic powers arise from this stage of practice?
premises: Knowledge of distant hearing is mentioned.
Paralysis of bonds is mentioned.
These are presented as resulting attainments.
items.inference: This practice yields knowledge of distant hearing and the power to paralyze bonds.
uncertainties: pāśa stobha may mean arresting bonds or immobilizing enemies
items.plain_english: O beloved, one gains knowledge of hearing from afar and likewise the power to paralyze bonds.

items.question: What further attainments are briefly attributed to this practice?
premises: Immortality is named as an attainment.
Transformation is named as an attainment.
The teaching states these results in brief.
items.inference: In brief, the practice brings immortality and transformation.
uncertainties: parivartanam may refer to bodily or situational transformation
items.plain_english: Likewise, O goddess, in brief one attains immortality and transformation.

items.question: How is the second eight-petaled locus characterized in meditation?
premises: A second locus is introduced.
It is described as eight-petaled.
It is brightly illuminated through meditation on fire.
items.inference: The second eight-petaled locus is characterized as well illuminated by fiery meditation.
items.plain_english: The second is an eight-petaled lotus, well illuminated by meditation on fire.

items.question: What ability arises for one whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation?
premises: The mind becomes absorbed in one-pointed meditation.
Such absorption enables creative power.
The practitioner can produce forms in many ways.
items.inference: One whose mind is fixed in one-pointed meditation can assume or create many forms.
items.plain_english: One whose mind is absorbed in one-pointed meditation can create many forms.

items.question: What destructive power is attributed to the practitioner when angered?
premises: The practitioner is described as angry.
The power to destroy is asserted.
The scope includes the entire triple world, moving and unmoving.
items.inference: When angered, the practitioner may destroy the whole triple world with all moving and unmoving beings.
items.plain_english: But when angered, he can destroy the entire triple world, with all that moves and does not move.

items.question: What liberating function is attributed to the third great wheel?
premises: A third great wheel is introduced.
It is associated with nine principles.
It is described as a liberator.
items.inference: The third great wheel functions as the liberator from the nine principles.
uncertainties: nava tattva may refer to a specific set of nine principles in this system
items.plain_english: The third great wheel is the liberator from the nine principles.

items.question: What bodily and perceptual powers result from this yogic attainment?
premises: Destruction of wrinkles and grey hair is mentioned.
Seeing from very far away is mentioned.
Both are presented as resulting powers.
items.inference: This attainment removes wrinkles and grey hair and grants vision from very far away.
items.plain_english: One gains the removal of wrinkles and grey hair, and likewise the ability to see from very far away.

items.question: How should a devoted practitioner cultivate multiple forms in solitude?
premises: The practice is to be done in solitude.
The practitioner should be intent on meditation.
The instruction is to create many forms.
items.inference: In solitude, one intent on meditation should create many forms.
items.plain_english: In solitude, intent on meditation, create many forms.

items.question: What result comes to one devoted to constant practice?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to constant practice.
Immortality is stated as an outcome.
The statement is presented as certain.
items.inference: One devoted to constant practice attains immortality.
items.plain_english: Indeed, one who is devoted to constant practice attains immortality.

items.question: How does abstaining from food by day affect age and death?
premises: Non-eating by day is specified as a practice.
Age and death are presented as something to be overcome.
The verse states a future outcome.
items.inference: Through abstaining from food by day, one will overcome death associated with age.
uncertainties: the exact sense of gamiṣyate with mṛtyuṃ is contextually interpretive
items.plain_english: By abstaining from food during the day, one will overcome the death of old age.

items.question: What bodily form results from constant yogic practice over sixteen years?
premises: The practice is constant yogic discipline.
The duration specified is sixteen years.
A specific bodily form is said to result.
items.inference: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.
uncertainties: dvi aṣṭa varṣa ākṛtiḥ is taken as the appearance of sixteen years
items.plain_english: Through constant yogic practice, one may attain the form of a sixteen-year-old.

items.question: What power arises from constantly contemplating a smoke-colored form?
premises: A smoke-colored object is to be contemplated always.
Contemplation yields a powerful effect.
The triple world can be shaken by this power.
items.inference: By always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one may shake the triple world.
items.plain_english: O beloved, by always contemplating a smoke-colored form, one can shake the triple world.
